blocks.text: 3-1 Collecting Data
Resources of collecting data; Methods of collecting data; How to select a sample; Types of samples
Key term: Primary resources
Key term: Secondary resources
Key term: Method of mass population
Key term: Method of sample
Key term: Biased choice
Key term: Random choice sample
Key term: Random sample
Key term: Layer sample

The method of collecting data is considered one of the most important phases that statistical research mainly depends on. Collecting data in such scientific methods will lead to get accurate outcomes when doing operations of statistical inferrence and proper decision making.
Resources of collecting data

Primary resources (Field resources) are the resources from which we originally get data through interviewing or questionnaires (survey). This type is distinguished by accuracy, but it needs time and effort and is highly expensive to conduct.

Secondary resources (historical resources): we can get data from authorities and agencies that formally work, such as the central agency for mobilization and statistics, internet and media. This type is a good type of resource because it saves time and money.
The method of collecting data
The method of collecting data is determined according to the aim and the size of the statistical society under study.
For example: The students of a school represent a statistical society whose value is the student.
First: Method of mass population:

Method of mass population means collecting the data related to the phenomenon of the statistical society. It is used to include all the society, such as the population. It includes all the values and is unbiased, and the outcomes are very accurate.
The disadvantages of such a method are: it needs long time and great efforts. Furthermore, it costs much money.
Second: Mehods of samples:
It mainly depends upon selecting a sample from the statistical society that it represents.
We conduct researches on the sample. The outcomes we get are generalized on the whole society.
Advantages of using methods of samples:
Advantage 1: using samples saves time, efforts and money.
Advantage 2: it is the only way to collect data about gigantic societies (like fish).
Advantage 3: it is the only method to study some limited societies, such as the two cases below.
A: Check the patient's blood by getting a sample (checking the whole blood leads to death).
B: Check the production of a factory producing electric lamps to determine the validity of the lamp (know for how long the lamp can be used before getting burned).
A disadvantage of sample methods: outcomes are not accurate if the selected sample doesn't represent all the society well; in such a case the sample is called biased.
How we select samples and the conditions must be found in getting a sample:
First: the biased selction (samples are not randomly selected)
Biased selection means selecting the sample in a way to satisfy the objectives of the research; this is called a deliberate sample.

For example, when we want to know how the students understood a lesson in mathematics we must analyze the outcomes of the test by considering the outcomes of a group of students studied the same topic without the other students; this is not a random selection.
Second: Random seclecion (random samples)
Random selection means selecting a sample such that the chance of getting any value from the society is equal.
Of the most important types of the random samples:
1. Simple random sample: the simplest type of sample; it can be got from homogeneous societies where selection is related to the size and number of units in the society.

A. If the size of the society is small: when choosing 5 students of a 40-student class, prepare an identical card for each student with name or number, put them in a box, draw a card randomly and return it again; repeat until the sample needed is obtained.

If the size of the society is big (e.g. selecting a sample of 5 students from 800): number the students from 1 to 800, then use the calculator or Excel to give 10 random digits in the field from 0.000 to 0.999, remove the decimal point so the field runs from zero to 999, and discard the digits that are more than 800.
Repeat pressing on the = key; the appearance of numbers will be successive.
Five non-repeated digits are enough to give the numbers of the sample of students.

When the society to be examined is heterogeneous or made up of qualitative sets that differ in characteristics, it is divided into homogeneous sets according to the characteristics forming it. Each set is called a layer, and the researcher selects a random sample in which each layer is represented according to its size in the society. Such a sample is called the layer sample.

For example: to study the educational level of a society of 400 persons where the ratio of males to females is 3:2, with a sample of 50 persons, we must select 30 persons from the male layer and 20 persons from the female layer randomly.

blocks.text: Lesson 3-2 Dispersion
Dispersions (Range- standard deviation)
Key term: Central tendency
Key term: Mean
Key term: Dispersion
Key term: Range
Key term: Standard deviation
Think and Discuss

You have previously learned the central tendency (mean - domain - mode) and used them to calculate a set of data to identify one value describing the trend of these data in centeralization around this value.
If the weekly wages in pounds of two sets of workers A and B in a factory are as follows: Set A: 170, 180, 180, 230, 240; Set B: 50, 180, 180, 190, 400
The mean = (total of these values) / (their number). $\text{The mean}=\dfrac{\text{Total of these values}}{\text{Their number}}$
Compare the wages of the two sets A and B to find :
1. The mean of wages for set A = the mean of wages of set B = LE 200
2. The median of wages = the mode wage = LE 180 for each set A and B
We notice that:
(1) The wages of the two sets are different but both have the same measures of central tendency.
(2) The wages of set A are close so the values are included between 170 and 240 pounds where the wages of set B are divergent so the values are included between 50 and 400 pounds.
i.e. The wages of set B is more divergent than the wages of set A.
So When we compare two sets, we must consider the dispersion of the values of both sets and being divergent from each other.
Dispersion of any set of values means divergence, or the differences between its values.
The dispersion is small if the differences between the values are little, whereas the dispersion is great if the differences between the values are very big.
When the dispersion is zero, all the values are equal.
The dispersion is a measure that expresses how homogeneous the sets are.
From the previous, we deduce:
To compare two or more sets of data, we must have a measure of central tendency and another measure of dispersion for each set.
Dispersions measurements
1 Range: (The simplest measure of dispersions)
The range is the difference between the greatest value and the smallest value in the set.
Notice that:
(1) The range is the simplest and easiest method of measuring dispersion.

(2) The range is influenced greatly by the outlier. The values of the second set disperse in a range of 50; when the last value (92) is removed the range = 52 - 42 = 10, or 1/5 of the previous range. $52-42=10=\frac{1}{5}\times 50$
(3) The range is not influenced by any value in the set except the greatest and smallest values, so it does not give a clear picture of the dispersion of the set.
2 Standard deviation :

Standard deviation is the commonest measure of dispersion and the most accurate (under certain conditions); it is the positive square root of the average of the squared deviations of the values from the mean.
Standard deviation σ equals the square root of (the sum of (x − x̄)² divided by n). $\sigma=\sqrt{\dfrac{\sum (x-\bar{x})^2}{n}}$
σ (sigma) denotes the standard deviation of the society (population) of data.
x̄ (x Bar) denotes the mean of the values of the society.
n denotes the number of values.
∑ denotes addition (summation).
First: calculating the standard deviation to a set of data:

Table of values x, deviations from the mean 16, and squared deviations, with Sum row (sum of x = 80, sum of squares = 54); sum cell under x - x̄ is blank. x, x - x̄, (x - x̄)² / 12, 12 - 16 = -4, 16 / 13, 13 - 16 = -3, 9 / 16, 16 - 16 = 0, zero / 18, 18 - 16 = 2, 4 / 21, 21 - 16 = 5, 25 / Sum 80, , 54
Second: Calculating the standard deviation to a frequency distribution :
For any frequency distribution :
For any frequency distribution, the standard deviation σ equals the square root of Σ(x - x̄)²k divided by Σk. $\sigma=\sqrt{\dfrac{\sum (x-\bar{x})^2 k}{\sum k}}$
x represents the value or the center of the set.
k represents the frequency of the value or the set.
Σk is the total of frequency. $\sum k$
x̄ is the mean, equal to Σxk divided by Σk. $\bar{x}=\dfrac{\sum xk}{\sum k}$

Step 3: Recall sum (standard deviation) (keys Shift 1 5 (VAR) 3 (X σn) =); then $\sigma \simeq 4.521$.
Step 4: Go back to the original system and switch off the calculator.
Notice that :
The standard deviation is affected by the deviations of all the values and its value is affected by the outlier.

The standard deviation has the same measuring units as the original data, so it is used to compare the dispersion of sets which have the same measuring units when the mean is equal. The set which contains more standard deviation is more dispersed.

worked_examples.question: The following frequency distribution shows the marks of 40 students in an exam (table). Find the standard deviation for this distribution.

steps.text: 1: Find the centers of sets x. Then: The center of the first set = (0+4)/2 = 2; the center of the second set = (4+8)/2 = 6; and then record them in the third column.
2: Multiply the centers of sets × its corresponding frequencies: i.e. x × k and record in the fourth column. Then find the mean $\bar{x} = \frac{\sum xk}{\sum k}$
3: Find the deviation of the center of each set (x) from the mean i.e. find $(x - \bar{x})$
4: Find squares of deviations of the center of each set from the mean: i.e $(x-\bar{x})^2$
5: Find the product of the square deviation of the center of each set from the mean × frequency of this set; i.e. $(x-\bar{x})^2 \times k$
6: Calculate the standard deviation $\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{\sum (x-\bar{x})^2 k}{\sum k}}$
